question.prompt: Name a fictional space station from a film, TV series, book or video game.
question.criteria: Any named fictional space station depicted in a film, TV series, book or video game counts, including mobile stations but not ordinary spacecraft or surface bases.

answers.evidence: The Death Star is the planet-destroying Imperial battle station introduced in Star Wars.
Deep Space Nine is the former Cardassian station that serves as the main setting of Star Trek: Deep Space Nine.
Babylon 5 is the diplomatic space station at the center of the television series of the same name.
The Citadel is an ancient space station that serves as a political hub in Mass Effect.
Omega is an asteroid-built space station featured in the Mass Effect games.
Sevastopol is the space station where most of Alien: Isolation takes place.
Talos I is the research station that serves as the setting of the 2017 game Prey.
Elysium is the luxurious orbital habitat inhabited by the wealthy in the film Elysium.
Cooper Station is the cylindrical space habitat shown near the end of Interstellar.
Tycho Station is a mobile construction station in The Expanse.
Space Station V is the rotating wheel-shaped station visited in 2001: A Space Odyssey.
Regula I is the orbital research station associated with Project Genesis in Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan.
Deep Space K-7 is the station visited in the Star Trek episode The Trouble with Tribbles.
The Watchtower is the Justice League's orbital headquarters in the animated series Justice League.
Yorktown is the vast Federation space station featured in Star Trek Beyond.
Earth Spacedock is the large orbital Starfleet facility introduced in Star Trek III: The Search for Spock.
Babylon 4 is the vanished predecessor station whose fate is explored in Babylon 5.
Empok Nor is an abandoned Cardassian space station featured in Star Trek: Deep Space Nine.
Thunderbird 5 is International Rescue's orbital monitoring station in Thunderbirds.
Satellite Five is the space station featured in the Doctor Who episode The Long Game.

question.explanation: Fictional space stations range from inhabited cities and trading hubs to military installations and planet-destroying battle stations.
